items.prompt: Why does a skipped-record count matter even when the accepted total is correct?
items.explanation: Partial acceptance can hide a data-quality failure unless the interface reports it. The application must decide whether continuing is allowed.

options.text: It proves rejected records are economically irrelevant
options.why: A programming policy does not prove a record has no economic meaning.

options.text: It makes partial acceptance visible for follow-up
options.why: The result can be mathematically correct for accepted data yet incomplete.

options.text: It repairs every rejected value without other information
options.why: Counting does not reconstruct the missing valid value.

options.text: It replaces the need for any input-validation policy
options.why: A count only makes sense after defining what is invalid.
